title: GRASP: A Disagreement Analysis Framework to Assess Group Associations in Perspectives

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring in-group cohesion and cross-group divergence (using metrics like Inter-Rater Reliability and Cross-Replication Reliability) of annotator perspectives on conversational safety across diverse racial and ethnic rater subgroups.
Calculating a Group Association Index (GAI) to evaluate systematic disagreements and alignment in subjective safety and offensiveness annotations among raters of different gender identities.

Comparing in-group and cross-group agreement on subjective natural language tasks (safety and offensiveness) across different rater age cohorts (e.g., GenZ, Millennial, GenX+, and distinct adult age brackets).

Evaluating rater disagreement and cohesion in social media offensiveness annotations among annotators from distinct geo-cultural regions (e.g., Arab Culture, Indian Cultural Sphere, Sinosphere, Western Europe).
Applying permutation tests and group association metrics to assess rater disagreement along intersectional demographic axes, such as combined race and gender or combined region and age subgroups.
